body:
Looking at the engine code, the underlying physics engine joint is being recreated when you exit and enter the tree.  However when it is recreated, the bodies are no longer in rest pose, so it gets set up all weird.

If I am correct, then you can workaround one of two ways:
* Reset your rigid body transforms to their original setting before entering the tree (so that the joint re-creates correctly)
* Use the physics server to set up the joints yourself using RID's rather than node paths. Then they can ignore the scene tree entirely.

### Notes on fixing this properly
This could be fixed in the engine for the local case with a continuity check before recreating a joint, but I think this is an architectural hack and the real fix requires an added PhysicsServer2D / 3D function.

The real source of the problem here is that the Joint2D node is not carrying its own rest pose data, whereas the underlying physics engine joint does. So the proper fix is (IMO):
- The Joint2D / Joint3D node base classes should store the local poses for their two connected bodies.
- The PhysicsServer2D/3D should allow the local poses to be sent through explicitly to set up the joint.

There may be quite a few benefits to doing this properly:
- It fixes other issues people are having where they can't set up joints without placing objects in their final locations in the scene
- It would allow joints to by dynamically disabled and then re-enabled using the PhysicsServer (or the nodes with added function)
- It allows serialisation of trees involving joints and bodies (barring any other serialisation issues)
